messages:
ellie: FYI customer wants an on‑prem POC but with embargoed images and a very tight upgrade/patch cadence (2h weekly maintenance window). They also want signed artifacts + SBOM. Can we do this without a large operations burden?
rahul: Quick clarifying Qs — are they asking for full air‑gapped delivery (tarball + manual import) or do they have an internal repo to pull from?
ellie: Manual import on their side. They can run a registry import job but nothing can reach the public internet.
rahul: OK. From packaging POV we can provide: (1) signed tarball with checksums, (2) detached signature + public key, (3) SBOM.json. Typical command we give ops: `sha256sum redwood-pkg-<ver>.tar.gz` and `gpg --verify redwood-pkg-<ver>.tar.gz.sig`.
tina: Two caveats: image size and upgrade delta. If we ship full bundles weekly it's heavy. We should offer a delta/patch bundle (binary diffs) for small patch windows. That reduces transfer and import time.
ellie: Customer insisted on a short maintenance window — 2 hours — so install time matters. Any estimates on import + startup time for a 1.3GB bundle vs a delta?
tina: Rough ballpark: 1.3GB gzipped tarball -> ~10–15 mins to copy on 1Gbps LAN + 8–20 mins for extract and load depending on node IO; service warmup can be parallelized but best to plan 30–40 mins end‑to‑end. Delta patch could drop that to sub‑10 mins for copy + <10 mins apply.
mike: Security questions: they require artifact signing with customer HSM-backed key or our signature? If they want to use their HSM to sign, we need to provide the signing payload and a signing API contract (detached signature over artifact + canonical SBOM). Also they ask for audited SBOM and alpine/os packages pinned.
rahul: We can support two modes: (A) Redwood signs and we provide revocation/expiry info, (B) we provide a canonical payload for them to sign with on‑prem HSM. Mode B needs a one-time schema agreement.
ellie: Pricing/contract Q from customer: will deltas be included in enterprise pricing or charged per GB? Sales would like guidance to reply.
rahul: For Dedicated/Private we usually include delta updates as part of the support contract; large full‑bundle deliveries might count toward bandwidth/ops surcharge for very frequent (weekly) pushes. Recommend offering 6 months of weekly deltas in PoC and then re-evaluate.
tina: Operational ask: we need an automated import script that runs on their airgapped bastion. Suggest we deliver `redwood-import.sh` (simple, idempotent) + a dry-run flag. Example snippet: ```#!/bin/bash
set -e
FILE=$1
sha256sum -c ${FILE}.sha256
gpg --batch --verify ${FILE}.sig ${FILE}
./apply-delta.sh ${FILE}
```
ellie: Perfect. Can you add a doc describing rollback steps in case an apply fails? Customer insisted on safe rollback inside the 2h window.	ina: Yes — rollback strategy: snapshot registry, snapshot etcd, and a fast revert which replaces images/kv from snapshot. We'll write steps and timing estimates.
mike: Also add a KMS key rotation note: if they sign with their key, rotating keys should be documented and we should support re-signing of the active bundle.
deploy-bot: artifact-upload: redwood-pkg-2026-05-01.tar.gz uploaded to private S3 (etag: abc123) — staging manifest generated. :white_check_mark:
ellie: Good — I'll pass this to the customer with: list of deliverables (signed tarball, SBOM, import script, rollback doc, cadence proposal) + pricing note (delta included for PoC, surcharge for weekly full bundles).
rahul: I'll draft the technical appendix for the contract: signing schema, delta format, apply/rollback steps, and expected timelines.
ellie: Thanks all. If we can lock the signing mode by EOD we can finalize the SOW. :thumbsup:
